quotes.text: Policies move at the speed of a committee but oversharing moves at the speed of business.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: So what does working governance look like once we strip away the theater? In one sentence, governance only works when it is embedded, enforced and measurable.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core framework in a single memorable sentence.

quotes.text: A policy tells people what they should do, but a guardrail changes what they can do by making the secure path the normal path.

quotes.text: The principle here is simple. Privileged access should exist for specific tasks, not for professional status.

chapters.title: Why oversharing beats every policy deck
Move one: auto-labeling and mandatory protection
Move two: DLP as an active control plane
Move three: temporary privileged access with Entra
What to mandate in 30 days and what not to do

takeaways: Governance only works when it is embedded in the flow of work, enforced by the platform and measurable through the share of sensitive data that is correctly labeled and protected.
Auto-labeling with mandatory protection and real-time DLP that warns, blocks or requires justification replace manual policing and awareness campaigns.
Purview and Entra form one control model, so privileged admin roles should be temporary and managed through PIM with approval and expiry.
hook: Many Microsoft 365 governance programs look mature on paper while oversharing quietly spreads sensitive files, and Copilot now surfaces that exposure at machine speed. This episode gives CIOs, CISOs and Microsoft 365 owners one framework, one executive metric and three concrete moves with Purview, DLP and Entra to make governance automatic instead of optional.
